The confidence intervals, on the other hand, reflect a growing uncertainty with longer time horizons. The 1-day interval, ranging from 374.84 to 390.66, primarily accounts for typical daily market volatility, immediate news impacts, and routine trading activity. As we extend to the 1-week horizon, the interval expands significantly to 367.29 to 402.71, incorporating potential shifts driven by weekly economic data releases, broader market sentiment changes, or more substantial news cycles. Despite the comprehensive range of probable outcomes captured by these confidence intervals, certain highly unpredictable events could push actual results beyond these stated boundaries. These include "black swan" events such as a sudden and severe global economic recession or an unexpected boom that significantly alters economic fundamentals. Major geopolitical conflicts escalating rapidly, unforeseen regulatory changes impacting entire industries, or disruptive technological breakthroughs could also dramatically alter market dynamics in ways not captured by historical volatility models. Such events, by their very nature, are difficult to quantify within standard probabilistic forecasts, as they represent deviations from typical market behavior and often carry an outsized impact that could drive values well outside the 90% confidence range.
